newsitem.title: UK: LVMH to buy Guinness interests in ventures.
newsitem.headline: LVMH to buy Guinness interests in ventures.

text.p: France's LVMH said on Wednesday it planned to exercise its option to buy Guinness Plc's interests in all the companies' joint ventures should Guinness complete its planned merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc.

The French drinks and luxury goods group, which held an estimated 14.2 percent stake in Guinness, reiterated its opposition to the Guinness-GrandMet deal, which would create a food and drinks giant worth more than 20 billion pounds ($32.6 billion).
LVMH said it had previously proposed that Guinness separate its beer activities from its spirits operations to create a leading wines and spirits group with LVMH.
"In response to the proposed merger, a similar proposal was made to Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, and this proposal remains open for discussion," LVMH said in a statement released here.
The company argued that within Guinness and GrandMet, only wines and spirits were clearly complementary.
"LVMH does not believe that shareholder value will be maximised by creating a conglomerate combining certain businesses with no common thread," the firm said.
LVMH said it believed the merger would create a "control event" that would allow it to exercise its option to buy Guinness' interests in their joint ventures at net asset value.
LVMH said it also had the option to buy back Guinness' 34 percent stake in Moet Hennessy at a discounted price.
LVMH said it would operate the ventures independently.

As a result, LVMH said it would have the right to continue marketing and distributing Guinness brands under existing agreements in key markets such as China, the U.S., France, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan and Thailand for at least 10 years.
Guinness and GrandMet have defended their plan to merge by saying that they have a range of highly complementary brands with very few overlapping products.
Their combined company would be called GMG Brands.
